questions.qtext: Select the correct statements with reference to a radio receiver:

options.text: Selectivity is the receiver’s ability to distinguish between two adjacent carrier frequencies.
Sensitivity is the ability of a receiver to detect weakest possible signal.
Fidelity is the ability of a receiver to reproduce faithfully all frequency components present in the baseband signals.
Double spotting in a radio receiver refers to the phenomenon when signals from the same short waves station is picked at two nearby points on the receiver tuning dial.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c, d)
• Sensitivity is the ability of a receiver to detect the weakest possible signal.
• Selectivity is the receiver’s ability to distinguish between two adjacent carrier frequencies.
• Fidelity is the ability of a receiver to reproduce faithfully all frequency components present in
the baseband signal.
• Double spotting in a radio receiver refers to the phenomenon when signals from the same
short waves station is picked at two nearby points on the receiver tuning dial.
